```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4, out.width = "100%",
                      fig.align = "center")
```

# 1. Data

```{r data}
library(fpp2)
library(ggplot2)
data("departures")
x=departures[,1]
x%>%autoplot()+theme_bw()+xlab("Years")+ ylab("Departures")
```

> **Comment:** The series has a clear upward trend (especially after 1998) and a 12-month seasonal pattern whose size grows over time, so it is not stationary and needs both a regular and a seasonal difference.

# 2. Automatic model (`auto.arima`)

```{r auto}
library(forecast)
m0<-auto.arima(x)
m0
```

> **Comment:** `auto.arima` selects the "airline" model ARIMA(0,1,1)(0,1,1)[12], whose two MA coefficients are clearly significant ($|\text{estimate}/\text{s.e.}| \approx 12.0$ and $9.7$, far above 1.96), and its AIC of 266.9 is the benchmark for the manual search below.

# 3. Differenced series

```{r diff}
library(latex2exp)
x%>%diff(12)%>%diff(1)%>%autoplot()+theme_bw()+ylab(TeX("$(1-B)(1-B^{12})X_t$"))+xlab("")
```

> **Comment:** After applying $(1-B)(1-B^{12})$ the trend and seasonality are gone and the series fluctuates around zero, although its variance looks somewhat larger after 2005.

# 4. Unit root tests

## ADF test

```{r adf}
library(urca)
t1=x%>%diff(12)%>%diff(1)%>%ur.df(lags = 6,type="none")
summary(t1)
```

> **Comment:** The ADF statistic ($-11.48$) is far below the 1% critical value ($-2.58$), so we reject the null hypothesis of a unit root: the differenced series is stationary.

## KPSS test

```{r kpss}
library(urca)
t2=x%>%diff(12)%>%diff(1)%>%ur.kpss(type="mu")
summary(t2)
```

> **Comment:** The KPSS statistic (0.0221) is well below even the 10% critical value (0.347), so we do not reject the null hypothesis of stationarity, which confirms the ADF result.

# 5. ACF and PACF

```{r acf}
x%>%diff(12)%>%diff(1)%>%ggAcf()+theme_bw()
```

```{r pacf}
x%>%diff(12)%>%diff(1)%>%ggPacf()+theme_bw()
```

> **Comment:** The ACF has strong significant spikes at lag 1 ($\approx -0.41$) and lag 12 ($\approx -0.30$) while the PACF decays more slowly (lags 1, 2, 12, 24), pointing to a non-seasonal MA(1) plus a seasonal MA(1), with smaller spikes around lags 5--7 and 11--13 justifying a search over higher AR/MA orders.

# 6. Fitting 256 candidate SARIMA models

```{r grid, cache=TRUE}
qQ=list()
for(i in 1:14) qQ[[i]]=c(i-1,0)
qQ[[15]]=c(0,1)
qQ[[16]]=c(1,1)
pP=qQ

dt_params=c()
for(i in 1:16){
    for(j in 1:16){
        temp=c(pP[[i]][1],1,qQ[[j]][1],pP[[i]][2],1,qQ[[j]][2],12)
        dt_params=rbind(temp,dt_params)
    }
}
colnames(dt_params)=c("p","d","q","P","D","Q","T")
rownames(dt_params)=1:256
models=vector("list",256)
for(i in 1:256){
  try(models[[i]]<-Arima(x,order = dt_params[i,1:3],
                          seasonal = list(order=dt_params[i,4:6],period=12),
                          lambda = NULL))
}
```

> **Comment:** 248 of the 256 candidate models were fitted; the 8 errors ("non-stationary AR part from CSS") come from high-order AR models whose starting estimates are not stationary, and `try()` simply skips them.

# 7. Residual check (Box-Pierce) and AIC table

```{r table}
library(caschrono)
aa=rep(NA,256)
for(i in 1:256){
    if(length(models[[i]]$residuals)>1){
        a=Box.test.2(x = models[[i]]$residuals,nlag = 10,type = "Box-Pierce")
        z=prod(1-(a[,2]<.05))
        if(z==1) aa[i]="y"
        else aa[i]="n"
    }
}
dt_params2=data.frame(dt_params)
dt_params2$residuals=aa
aic=rep(NA,256)
model_names=rep(NA,256)
for(i in 1:256){
    if(length(models[[i]]$aic)>0){
        aic[i]=models[[i]]$aic
        model_names[i]=as.character(models[[i]])
    }
}
dt_params2$aic=aic
dt_params2$model=model_names
library(DT)
dt_params2$aic=round(dt_params2$aic,4)
dt_params2=na.omit(dt_params2)
# A PDF cannot hold the interactive DT table, so print a plain table instead
knitr::kable(dt_params2, row.names = FALSE)
```

> **Comment:** The Box-Pierce test (lags 1 to 10) does not reject white-noise residuals for 237 of the 248 models (residuals = "y"); the 11 failures are all simple models with no non-seasonal MA term, and the lowest AIC (255.66) belongs to the heavily parameterised ARIMA(8,1,12)(0,1,0)[12].

# 8. Best models (AIC < 260) and coefficient significance

```{r best}
i=as.numeric(rownames(dt_params2)[which(dt_params2$aic<260)])
res=sapply(i, function(x)as.character(models[[x]]))
res
x_test=sapply(i, function(x)t_stat(models[[x]]))
bb=rep(NA,16)
for(j in 1:16){
    temp=t(x_test[[j]])[,2]
    z=prod((temp<.05))
    bb[j]=z
}
bb
as.character(models[[i[length(i)-1]]])
```

> **Comment:** 17 models have AIC < 260 (all with white-noise residuals), but among the 16 checked in `bb` only SARIMA(3,1,1)(0,1,1)[12] has every coefficient significant at the 5% level, so this simple 5-parameter model (AIC = 256.66, third lowest and well below auto.arima's 266.9) is selected.

# 9. Train / forecast

```{r forecast, fig.height=3.4}
x_tr <- window(x,end=2009)
fit <- Arima(x_tr,order = c(3,1,1),
              seasonal = list(order=c(0,1,1),period=12),
              lambda = NULL)
f_fit<-forecast(fit)
autoplot(x_tr, series="Data") +
    autolayer(fit$fitted, series="SARIMA(3,1,1)(0,1,1)[12]") +
    autolayer(f_fit, series="Prediction") +
    xlab("Year") + ylab("Departures") + ggtitle("Permanent Departures") + theme_bw()+theme(legend.title = element_blank(),legend.position = "bottom")
```

> **Comment:** Fitted on data up to 2009, the SARIMA(3,1,1)(0,1,1)[12] model tracks the observed series closely, and its 24-month forecast continues the upward trend and seasonal peaks, with prediction intervals that widen further into the future.
